AI Money Coach

A calm, judgement-free coach for everyday money: where it goes, how to pay debt down and how to save without feeling broke. It works with your real numbers and keeps things simple.

TL;DR
  • Best for budgets, debt payoff plans and saving habits.
  • Give it monthly income, fixed costs and debts with interest rates.
  • It is a coach, not a licensed adviser: check loans, investments and taxes with a professional.
Not financial advice

The Money Coach helps you think about budgets, debt and savings habits. It does not know your full situation and is not a licensed adviser. Check big decisions such as loans, investments and taxes with a qualified professional.

What this coach helps with

  • Building a simple monthly budget
  • Choosing which debt to pay off first
  • Finding spending leaks
  • Setting up an emergency fund
  • Planning for a big purchase or a gap in income

Prompts you can copy

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

  1. Act as my money coach. My monthly income is [income]. My fixed costs are [list]. Build me a simple budget with saving as the first line, not the last.

  2. Here are my debts with balances and interest rates: [list]. Show me the avalanche and snowball order and how long each plan takes at [amount] a month.

  3. Here is last month's spending: [list or categories]. Find the three biggest leaks and suggest a realistic cut for each.

  4. I want an emergency fund of [amount]. I can save [amount] a month. Make a plan with milestones and what to do if I miss a month.

  5. I get paid irregularly, between [low] and [high] a month. Help me build a budget that works in a bad month.

  6. I want to buy [item] for [price] in [months]. Is that realistic on my budget? If not, what would make it realistic?

  7. Ask me 6 questions to understand my money habits, then tell me which one habit to change first.

  8. Write a short script for talking to my partner about money without it turning into a fight. Our main issue is [issue].

  9. Explain [term, e.g. compound interest] with a simple example using my numbers: [numbers].

  10. Make a 30-day no-spend challenge for me that still allows [essentials], with a small reward at the end.

  11. I just got [bonus or extra money]. Help me decide how to split it between debt, savings and something fun.

  12. Turn our chat into a one-page money plan: monthly budget, debt order, savings goal and the first three actions.

Two example conversations

Written by the Intellect AI team to show the style of answers. Not a real user conversation.

ExampleTwo debts, one plan

YouI have $1,800 on a credit card at 24% and a $4,000 personal loan at 11%. I can pay $350 a month in total.

Money CoachPay the minimums on both and put everything else on the credit card first, since its rate is more than double. At $350 a month the card is gone in roughly 6 months; then the full $350 goes to the loan. Want me to lay it out month by month?

ExampleSaving on an irregular income

YouI'm a freelancer. Some months I earn $3,000, some only $1,200. I never manage to save.

Money CoachBuild your budget on the bad month: $1,200. In every good month, anything above that goes first to a buffer account until it holds one bad month of costs, then to savings. That way a slow month stops being an emergency. What do your fixed costs add up to?

Tips for better answers

  • Use rough numbers if you don't know exact ones. A budget built on estimates beats no budget.
  • Ask for the plan as a table so you can copy it into a spreadsheet or notes.
  • Tell the coach what you refuse to cut. Plans that ignore your priorities don't last.
  • Never paste card numbers, bank logins or ID documents into any chat.

Questions people ask

Is an AI money coach the same as a financial adviser?

No. An AI money coach helps you organise your own numbers, compare simple options like debt payoff orders and build habits. It is not licensed, does not see your full situation and cannot take responsibility for advice. For investments, loans, pensions and taxes, check with a qualified financial professional in your country.

What is the fastest way to pay off debt?

Mathematically, the avalanche method is fastest: pay minimums on everything and put extra money on the debt with the highest interest rate. The snowball method pays the smallest balance first, which costs a little more but gives quick wins. Ask the coach to compare both with your real numbers.

How big should my emergency fund be?

A common rule of thumb is three to six months of essential costs, but any buffer helps. Many people start with one month of rent and food, then grow it. If your income is irregular, aim higher. The coach can turn your target into a monthly amount and a realistic date.

What information should I share with the money coach?

Share monthly income, fixed costs like rent and transport, debts with balances and interest rates, and your goals. Round numbers are fine. Never share card numbers, account logins, passwords or ID documents. The coach only needs the shape of your finances, not access to them.
